structure.heading: How we are organised
structure.lead: Each body of the Student Government has its own task. Some represent students and handle day-to-day matters, others adopt the rules, check that they are followed or run elections. All of them work under the Student Government Regulations.

chair.name: Student Government Chair
chair.role: Represents all students of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business at the University and beyond, including as a member of the University Council. Leads the work of the Board and the University Student Government Council. Appoints 2 to 3 Vice-Chairs and assigns them specific areas.

board.name: Board
board.role: The executive body, headed by the Chair. It handles the Student Government's day-to-day work and carries out the Council's resolutions. Each Board member is responsible for an area: administration, teaching and quality of education, finance, external relations, promotion, human resources and the Jelenia Góra branch.

russ.name: University Student Government Council
russ.role: The Student Government's highest law-making body. It adopts the Student Government's regulations and budget, elects the Chair and approves the Board. It agrees the study regulations, gives its opinion on scholarship rules and takes positions on matters that concern students.

audit.name: Audit Committee
audit.role: A three-member supervisory body. It handles student complaints about the Student Government's bodies, checks how the budget is spent and rules on the validity of elections and Council votes.

election.name: Student Electoral Committee
election.role: A three-member electoral body. It sets the election calendar, prepares voter lists, organises the vote and makes sure it runs properly. Its members cannot stand as candidates.

branch.name: Jelenia Góra Branch Student Government
branch.role: Represents students of the UEW branch in Jelenia Góra and builds academic life on site.

center.role: The Student Government's bodies act on behalf of all students of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business. You can vote in their elections, stand as a candidate or join one of the project teams when recruitment opens.

adapciak.signature: Your first friendships begin before the first lecture.
adapciak.desc: An eight-day camp for first-years in the last free days before the academic year starts. It begins on Sunday morning on campus with a welcome and a field game, and then you all leave Wrocław together. Pool parties and field games await, every evening ends with a themed party, and at the end we reward the winning groups. So on your first day of classes you don't walk onto campus as a stranger.

dni.signature: You don't have to “somehow find out”. We show you the University from the inside.
dni.desc: Two days of talks and training for first-years. On day one you learn, among other things, how a test differs from an exam, what the academic quarter is and what the Dean does. On day two we walk around campus together and show you the key places. Part-time students have online sessions. After each day you can meet others at the afterparty at Zaprzegubie or at UE Party.

party.signature: A community needs shared fun as much as shared work.
party.desc: A series of parties for students of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business and the whole student community of Wrocław. A regular break from classes and exams, and during the Adaptation Days one of the places where first-years get to know each other.

facts.v: students of the University and all of Wrocław

animalia.signature: Having fun has a concrete result here: support for one chosen species.
animalia.desc: A charity project raising money to save endangered species. Each year we choose one animal from those cared for by the DODO Foundation at Wrocław ZOO, and the money raised goes to it. The first day takes place at the ZOO, with stations of games, puzzles and face painting for children. The second is an evening for students with a concert, dance workshops and an auction of vouchers and gadgets.

facts.v: a day at the ZOO and an evening for students

bal.signature: One night when different generations of the University meet at one table.
bal.desc: An evening the Student Government organises for students, staff, alumni and friends of the University, attended by the University Authorities. It opens with an official welcome and dinner, followed by dance and acrobatics shows, performances and a photo wall. The “Ekonomki” statuettes go to lecturers nominated by students, and at the end we choose the King and Queen of the night.

facts.v: after signing up via a form

mosty.signature: Sometimes the shortest route to a new perspective runs through another university.
mosty.desc: An exchange between students of five partner universities of economics in Poland. It was started in 2005 by the student governments of SGH Warsaw School of Economics and Wroclaw University of Economics and Business. For four days you take part in talks, workshops and a field game and see up close what studying in another city is like. Evenings are for socialising, and in Wrocław a party on a boat is a fixed part of the programme.

test.signature: Economics leaves the exam room and becomes a shared event.
test.desc: A competition modelled on Polish Television's Great Test, co-run by the student governments of five universities of economics together with the Forum of Economic Universities. The regional round takes place on the same day in all five cities: about 100 people at each university answer economics questions in an app, with a coffee break halfway through. The top five from each city go on to the national final, held in a different partner city each year.

tedx.signature: One stage, and ideas meant to stay with you.
tedx.desc: A local stage in the TEDx format: independent events held around the world around ideas worth spreading. Speakers who live their passion have a few minutes to plant an idea in you through a story. Between talks there are workshops with partner companies, and in the evening a Cocktail Party where you can talk to the speakers.

graduetion.signature: Your diploma becomes a shared rite of passage, not a document from a counter.
graduetion.desc: A graduation celebration inspired by American traditions. The morning is the official part: the graduation ceremony in gowns and caps, speeches by the University Authorities and the Student Government Chair, a mini poll and photos on campus. The most emotional moment is throwing the caps: the end of one chapter and the start of the next. In the evening you celebrate away from the University.

juwenalia.signature: One festival for students of every university in Wrocław.
juwenalia.desc: Wrocław Juwenalia are organised jointly by the student governments of Wrocław's universities, including ours. Every year they draw thousands of students and local residents. The highlight is two days of concerts at Pola Osobowickie with the biggest Polish artists, and next to the stage there is a zone with attractions, food, a chill-out area and an electronic stage.

prawaStudenta.metaDesc: Know your rights at Wroclaw University of Economics and Business: from an individual study arrangement to a board exam. The Study Regulations made simple.
prawaStudenta.heroLead: Studying isn't only duties. Get to know the rights you have at every stage, and where to find support when someone breaks them.
prawaStudenta.heading: Every student has the right to know their rights
prawaStudenta.intro: At the start of the academic year, during the Adaptation Days, the Student Government runs training on students' rights and duties for first-year students. The Study Regulations list 25 rights - below we describe the seven students ask about most.

repeat.title: Repeating classes
repeat.desc: If you do not pass a semester, the Dean may let you continue conditionally or repeat the semester.
repeat.expl: Within 10 days of the end of the resit session, apply to the Dean for conditional enrolment (you repeat the subject while moving on) or to repeat the semester. No justification is needed. You get conditional enrolment if you are missing only a few ECTS credits - the Dean decides whether the shortfall is too large. You can repeat the same subject at most twice.

ios.title: Individual study plan
ios.desc: A different group for selected subjects and, in special situations, an individual way of passing classes.
ios.expl: Are you active in research, sport or the Student Government, do you have a disability, are you pregnant, a parent, or caring for someone close? The Dean may let you attend selected subjects with a different group and, in special situations, pass classes individually.

absence.title: Excused absence
absence.desc: The right to have an absence excused, get a new exam date and take leave from classes.
absence.expl: Show your documents to the teacher within 14 days, and to the examiner within 3 days of the cause ending. The examiner will set a new date. For a longer break you can take leave: short-term for up to a month or long-term for two semesters.

change.title: Changing your field of study
change.desc: You can move to another programme if you meet its admission requirements.
change.expl: The Dean decides on a change of programme. You must meet the new programme's admission requirements - the same as the students you are joining. Programmes differ, so the Dean sets which subjects you need to make up, how and by when. Subjects you have already passed can be recognised if their learning outcomes match the new programme.

ects.title: Transferring and recognising ECTS credits
ects.desc: Subjects passed at another university, including abroad, can be recognised together with their ECTS credits.
ects.expl: ECTS credits are how the law measures a student's average workload. One credit means 25-30 hours of work - classes plus independent study - and a semester is usually 30 credits. The Dean decides on recognising a subject from another university, including abroad (e.g. Erasmus), at your request, by comparing learning outcomes. Passing partial grades from subjects you did not complete at the University are recognised for 3 years.

commission.title: Board exam
commission.desc: If you think a grade is unfair, you can request a board exam or board assessment with an observer of your choice.
commission.expl: Think a grade is unfair? Within 2 working days of it being announced, apply to the Dean for a board exam or board assessment, with detailed reasons. The person who gave the grade does not sit on the board, and you can name an observer. The board's grade is final.

mode.title: Changing your study mode
mode.desc: You can move between full-time and part-time studies.
mode.expl: The Dean decides. You can move to full-time studies no earlier than after the 2nd semester (first cycle) or the 1st semester (second cycle), no later than two semesters before the end of studies, and with the average set by the Rector.

source.q: Where do my rights as a student come from?
source.a: From the Law on Higher Education and Science (Art. 75(3)) and the University Study Regulations (Section 4). The Regulations list 25 rights, including repeating classes, an individual study arrangement, leave and a board exam.

ios.q: What is an individual study plan (IOS)?
ios.a: It is the Dean's permission to attend selected subjects with a different group and, in special situations - disability, illness, parenthood or at the Student Government's request - to pass classes individually. It is available to, among others, students active in research, sport and the Student Government, parents and carers.

commission.q: Can I take a board exam?
commission.a: Yes, if you submit a reasoned application to the Dean within 2 working days of the grade being announced and the Dean agrees. You can name an observer, and the board's grade is final.

correction.title: Note on the older PDF infopack
correction.body: The PDF infopack gives fixed limits: three subjects and 25 ECTS. The current Regulations (Section 40) do not contain them - the Dean decides whether the ECTS shortfall is too large.

absence.label: Absence from class or an exam
absence.title: An absence must be explained within a set time
absence.summary: The teacher excuses a short absence from class or an assessment; an examiner handles an exam absence. The reason is assessed using documents provided by the student.
facts: You provide the teacher with the reason and documents within 14 days after the reason for absence ends.
For an examiner, the deadline is 3 days after the reason for absence ends.
Once accepted, the examiner sets an individual exam date and the teacher defines how missed work is made up.
The Dean excuses an absence from a diploma exam and sets a new date.

grades.label: Grades and percentage thresholds
grades.title: The same grading scale applies to assessments and exams
grades.summary: The Regulations connect each numerical grade with the achieved learning outcomes. When points are used, points may not be deducted for a wrong answer or no answer.
facts: 5.0: at least 90%; 4.5: 80% to under 90%.
Programmes with external accreditation may apply the accrediting institution’s requirements.

exams.label: Assessments, exams and results
exams.title: Dates and results should not arrive as a surprise
exams.summary: The Regulations set minimum notice periods for assessments and exam schedules, as well as deadlines for grades. Students must also check their grades in USOS.
facts: The date of a test other than an exam is announced at least 2 weeks in advance.
Exam dates are published no later than 4 weeks before the session starts.
Test results are given within 2 weeks, partial grades within 3 days of the last class, and exam results within 3 days.
You must be told about a failing grade no later than 3 days before the resit.
Check your final grades in USOS within 7 days of the end of the resit session.

conditional.label: Conditional progress or repeating a semester
conditional.title: Conditional progress is a Dean’s decision, not an automatic limit
conditional.summary: If you have not passed the semester, you may request conditional progress or permission to repeat it. The Regulations leave the assessment of an acceptable ECTS deficit to the Dean.
facts: Submit the request within 10 days after the resit session ends and all grades are in USOS.
A request for conditional progress or semester repetition does not require justification.
Conditional progress may be allowed if the Dean considers the ECTS deficit not excessive and no programme or legal obstacle applies.
As a rule, the same semester or course may not be repeated more than twice.

leave.label: Leave from classes
leave.title: Leave may be short- or long-term
leave.summary: At a student’s request, the Dean may grant leave when participation in classes is temporarily impossible. In some cases, selected courses may still be taken during leave.
facts: Short-term leave lasts up to one month; long-term leave generally lasts two semesters and exceptionally one.
Reasons include health, education or research, pregnancy or parenthood, financial hardship or a sudden serious event.
Apply immediately after the reason arises; leave cannot be granted for a completed semester.
The Dean may indicate courses to be completed during leave.

registration.label: Registration and supplementary subjects
registration.title: Registration takes place in USOS on dates set by the Dean
registration.summary: You register for subjects and groups of subjects in USOS. The number of humanities, social, foreign language and PE subjects and when you take them is set by your programme.
facts: Check the set of subjects you must take, including languages and PE, in the study programme for your field, level and year of admission.
Registration takes place in USOS on dates set by the Dean, announced at least 2 weeks in advance. Foreign language registration is run by the Foreign Language Centre.
If you miss a subject registration through no fault of your own, you can ask the Dean to register you.
If you do not register for a group of subjects, the Dean assigns you ex officio.
Withdrawing from a subject you registered for requires the Dean's consent.

applications.label: Applications and individual matters
applications.title: A good application starts with a specific request
applications.summary: As a rule, the Dean decides individual student matters. Before submitting an application, the Regulations advise checking the relevant rules and consulting the Dean’s Office.
facts: An application should contain a concise request and substantive - and if possible formal - justification.
Attach the documents required for the matter and those confirming the facts in your justification.
You get at least 7 days to fill in any gaps; if you do not, the application is left unexamined.
A simple decision should be issued within 14 days, and a matter needing clarification generally within a month.
If the Dean does not fully grant your request, you can appeal to the Rector within 7 days of receiving the decision.

grades.body: Your curriculum is complete and no missing grade blocks admission.

jsa.title: The JSA report was assessed by your supervisor
jsa.body: The PRP colour does not make a decision. Your supervisor reads the report and accepts the thesis or requests revision.
jsa.action: Wait for the report and supervisor decision. A thesis may undergo no more than two JSA checks.

reviews.title: Two positive reviews and clearance are complete
reviews.body: Reviews by the supervisor and reviewer plus University clearance open the path to the exam.
reviews.action: Check reviews and clearance in APD/USOS. Reviews should be available at least 2 working days before the exam.

approval.title: Green light 1 · APD
approval.body: Your supervisor accepted the thesis and sent it for review in APD.

grades.title: Green light 2 · USOS
grades.body: USOS contains every grade required by your curriculum. You need both green lights at once.

timeline.label: Process map
timeline.heading: Six stages, not a single upload
timeline.lead: Every state has a different owner and risk. Do not plan the defence as if everything happened instantly after upload.
timeline.mapNote: This is a responsibility map, not a copy of the APD interface. Select a stage to see its owner and the evidence that the process has actually moved on.
timeline.proofLabel: How to know this stage is complete

final.title: Final version
final.body: The supervisor confirms that a specific file may enter the formal process.
final.proof: The supervisor has clearly approved this version for submission, rather than merely sending another round of comments.

metadata.title: APD and metadata
metadata.body: You complete PL/EN data, accept the declaration and send the thesis to the supervisor.
metadata.proof: APD shows a complete thesis record, the correct file and a status confirming transfer to the supervisor.

similarity.title: JSA screening
similarity.body: APD sends the thesis to the national anti-plagiarism system and generates a report.
similarity.proof: A similarity report is attached to the thesis; the percentage alone does not yet mean approval.

decision.title: Supervisor decision
decision.body: The supervisor analyses the report, accepts the thesis or requests changes.
decision.proof: The thesis status confirms acceptance after JSA analysis or clearly requests a revision.

reviews.title: Reviews and clearance
reviews.body: Supervisor and reviewer submit reviews and the University confirms clearance.
reviews.proof: APD contains two reviews and University clearance no longer blocks admission to the exam.

defence.title: Diploma exam
defence.body: The date and three-person committee appear in APD at least 7 days in advance.
defence.proof: APD shows the date, place and three-person diploma examination committee.

deadlines.label: Deadline navigator
deadlines.heading: Choose your route
deadlines.lead: The dates below refer to 2025/2026 and are archived. Confirm the 2026/2027 deadlines with your Dean's Office before planning your thesis submission.
deadlines.warning: Missing the final deadline may result in removal from the student list. If you are near the boundary, do not rely on this page alone - contact your supervisor and the Dean's Office.

jsa.label: JSA lab
jsa.heading: Colour is a signal, not a verdict
jsa.lead: PRP helps the supervisor read the similarity report. It does not automatically assess authorship and cannot replace source analysis.
jsa.rule: The current rules allow no more than two JSA checks. The supervisor decides within 3 working days after receiving the report.

green.title: The report still needs to be read
green.body: A low PRP does not end the analysis. The supervisor checks where similarities come from and whether quotations and borrowed material are marked correctly.

orange.title: Similarities require careful analysis
orange.body: The result signals a larger share of similarity. The supervisor assesses its nature and decides whether the thesis proceeds or needs revision.

red.title: A high PRP requires a supervisor decision
red.body: This is a serious signal, but still not an automatic verdict. Do not try to ‘lower the percentage’; work with sources and supervisor feedback.

exam.label: Defence table simulator
exam.heading: Three people. Three angles.
exam.lead: The oral exam includes three questions. Instead of studying everything in the same way, prepare a separate strategy for each question type.
exam.notice: The date and committee should appear in APD at least 7 days before the exam.

chair.title: Can you place your thesis in the wider context of your programme?
chair.body: The question comes from the published topic list for your programme. It checks orientation in the discipline, not just recall of one definition.
chair.prepare: Work through the 40 or 50 topics and prepare a definition, relationships and one example for each.

promoter.title: Do you understand the concepts your thesis is built on?
promoter.body: The supervisor asks about the theoretical part, conceptual choices and literature. It tests understanding of your argument, not recitation of a chapter.
promoter.prepare: Explain the main concepts without quoting the text and justify why the chosen theory fits the problem.

reviewer.title: Can you defend the method, result and limitations?
reviewer.body: The reviewer focuses on the research problem, method, results and conclusions - including what the study does not prove.
reviewer.prepare: Practise a 90-second answer: objective → method → key finding → meaning → one limitation.

calculator.heading: See what really weighs on the result
calculator.lead: Enter your study average, two thesis grades and three exam question grades. The calculator uses the weights from the Study Regulations.
calculator.disclaimer: This simulates components and weights, not the official diploma grade. UEW determines the final result and its classification under the applicable rules.

register.label: Create an account

prepare.label: I am preparing for assessments or exams
prepare.title: Pass the class components before sitting the exam
prepare.summary: Passing every other component of the course is required for admission to the exam. A negative grade at the first attempt gives you a resit, but a positive exam grade cannot be improved.
prepare.signal: Control-test dates should be announced at least 2 weeks ahead, and exam dates no later than 4 weeks before the session.
actions: Review the requirements given during the first class.
Compare the exam timetable with all component assessments.
After every grade, check whether you are entitled to a resit.
checks: No more than four exams in one semester.
An unexcused absence results in a 2.0 grade.
One negative component grade makes the final course grade negative.

absence.label: I missed a test or an exam
absence.moment: the reason and a quick response matter
absence.title: An excused absence opens the way to an individual date
absence.summary: Give the teacher the reason and documents within 14 days, or the examiner within 3 days after the reason ends. If accepted, an individual date can be set.
absence.signal: If the new date falls after the relevant session ends, the Dean’s consent is required.
actions: Record the date on which the reason for your absence ended.
Send the explanation and evidence to the teacher or examiner.
If the date falls outside the session, submit a reasoned application to the Dean.
checks: The document supports a significant reason for the absence.
The message reached the right person on time.
You have a confirmed new date or instructions for an application.

missing.label: A grade is missing or incorrect
missing.title: Teacher first; after three working days, the Dean’s Office
missing.summary: You must verify final grades within 7 days after the resit session. Report a missing or inconsistent grade immediately to the teacher, who has up to 3 working days to correct it.
missing.signal: A missing entry is not the same as a failing grade - start the correction procedure first.
actions: Take a screenshot of the grade or empty field and record the date.
Write to the teacher with the course, group and correct grade.
If there is no entry or correction after 3 working days, notify the Dean’s Office.
checks: You are checking the final course grade, not only a component.
You have proof that the first report was sent.
Do not request conditional progression until every grade is entered in USOS.

dispute.label: I believe the grade is unfair
dispute.moment: after a first-attempt or resit grade is announced
dispute.title: A committee is not a third attempt - identify a concrete flaw
dispute.summary: The application may concern impartiality, inconsistency with the rules or scope given in the first class, or the conduct of the assessment or exam. The committee’s grade is final.
dispute.signal: A negative committee grade rules out conditional progression; requesting repetition of the semester remains possible.
actions: Record the exact date the disputed grade was announced.
Collect the requirements, your work and facts about the process.
Submit a detailed application within 2 working days.
checks: Your reasons describe a procedural concern, not only disappointment with the result.
You know that the committee chair decides the form.
You may nominate your own observer.

failed.label: I did not pass a subject or a semester
failed.moment: after all entries and the resit session
failed.title: Conditional progression and repetition are different decisions - both require an application
failed.summary: Conditional progression lets you continue while repeating failed courses if the Dean considers the ECTS deficit not excessive. Repeating the semester may also involve programme differences.
failed.signal: Apply only after every grade is entered in USOS, but no later than 10 days after the resit session. No justification is required.
actions: Check all grades and list failed courses with their ECTS.
Compare conditional progression with repeating the semester; the Dean decides eligibility.
Submit the correct USOS application, then verify the date, courses and fee in the decision.
checks: A negative committee result rules out conditional progression.
Repeating the first semester of first-cycle studies exceptionally requires the Rector’s consent.
Check the current fee in the order applicable to your cohort, not in an old PDF.

template.summary: A good application does not need to be long. §12 requires a concise and precise request, substantive and, where possible, formal grounds, plus documents supporting the facts described.
steps: Begin with “I request…”.
Briefly explain why the request is justified.
Name the attachments and legal basis if known.
Read the wording once more before submitting.
template.template:
I request [specific decision].

Grounds
[What happened? When? Why is it relevant?]

Attachments
1. [document name]
2. [document name]

conditional.label: Conditional continuation
conditional.title: Apply after all grades appear in USOS
conditional.summary: If you have not passed the semester, the Dean may allow continuation while you repeat failed courses. In the Dean’s assessment, the ECTS deficit must not be excessive.
checklist: Submission within 10 days after the resit session
steps: Wait until all grades are entered.
Choose conditional continuation.
Name the failed courses.
Submit without grounds within the regulatory deadline.
conditional.template: I request conditional permission to continue my studies in the next semester while repeating the following courses: [list].

repeat.label: Repeating a semester
repeat.title: Repeating a semester also requires an application
repeat.summary: The Dean may permit a semester to be repeated due to unsatisfactory results and will set how programme differences are made up. Repeating the first semester of a first-cycle programme exceptionally requires the Rector’s consent.
checklist: Application within 10 days after the resit session
steps: Choose the semester repetition application.
State the semester and failed courses.
Submit - no grounds are required.
After the decision, check the conditions and programme differences.
repeat.template: I request permission to repeat semester [number] due to unsatisfactory academic results.

ios.label: Individual study organisation (IOS)
ios.title: IOS changes organisation, not the study programme
ios.summary: IOS may allow a change of administrative group or an individual assessment mode in special circumstances. The seven-day deadline comes from the Infopack; §15 itself defines IOS scope and conditions.
checklist: Description of the reason for IOS
Initial consultation with the Dean’s Office
steps: Identify the adjustment you need.
Collect documents supporting your situation.
Apply as early in the semester as possible.
After approval, agree changes with teachers and notify the Dean’s Office.
ios.template:
I request individual study organisation in semester [semester], consisting of [group change / individual assessment mode].
Grounds: [situation and required adjustment].

ips.label: Individual study programme (IPS)
ips.title: IPS replaces courses under an academic supervisor
ips.summary: IPS lets you replace non-mandatory courses with others aligned with your development path without losing required learning outcomes. Detailed deadlines and the proposal form come from the Infopack and the circular it cites.
steps: Find an IPS supervisor.
Compare outcomes, content and ECTS.
Prepare the proposal using the current form.
Apply before the semester begins.
ips.template:
I request permission to follow an individual study programme in semester(s) [scope].
I propose replacing [course] with [class].
Development-path grounds: [description].

transfer.label: Transfer
transfer.title: Check the conditions and available place first
transfer.summary: A transfer may concern the university, programme, mode of study, course group or administrative group. Depending on the type, the Rector or Dean considers the application.
steps: Ask the Dean’s Office whether transfer is possible.
Check requirements and grade average where relevant.
State the reason and target programme or group.
Attach documents and submit.
transfer.template:
I request a transfer from [current programme/mode/group] to [target programme/mode/group] from semester [number].
Grounds: [specific reasons].

extension.label: Session extension
extension.title: A different exam date requires exceptional grounds
extension.deadline: Latest assessment date: 8 March or 28 September
extension.summary: The Dean may agree to assessments or exams at different dates only on a particularly justified application. The Regulations set final dates for winter and summer semesters.
steps: Contact the teacher.
Collect evidence of the obstacle.
Apply before the relevant final date.
After approval, agree the date with the teacher.
extension.template:
I request permission to take the [assessment/exam] in [course] on a date other than scheduled.
Reason: [detailed explanation].
Proposed date: [date].

recognition.label: Recognition of a course or grade
recognition.title: Compare one specific course with another
recognition.summary: The Dean assesses matching learning outcomes. For classes completed at another university, proof of completion and a syllabus are needed; separate levels apply to language certificates.
checklist: Names of previous and target courses
steps: Name the pair of courses to compare.
Obtain the full syllabus and proof of grade.
Attach them to the application.
Wait for the learning-outcome assessment.
recognition.template:
I request recognition of the subject [earlier subject, university] towards the subject [subject at the University].
The request is based on matching: [learning outcomes, content, hours, ECTS].

committee.label: Committee assessment or exam
committee.title: A review of fairness, not a third attempt
committee.deadline: You have 2 working days from publication of the disputed grade
committee.summary: The application must identify detailed concerns about impartiality, consistency with requirements or the conduct of the assessment. A negative committee grade rules out conditional continuation.
checklist: Requirements stated in the first class
steps: Record the publication date.
Collect materials supporting the objection.
Submit detailed grounds within 2 working days.
Await information about the committee and assessment form.
committee.template:
I request permission for a committee [assessment/exam] in [course].
The disputed grade was announced on [date].
My objection concerns [impartiality / requirements / conduct].
Grounds: [specific facts].

lateRegistration.label: Registration outside the system
lateRegistration.title: Explain why you missed the deadline through no fault of your own
lateRegistration.summary: §24 permits an application for course registration where the deadline was missed for reasons not attributable to the student. The Infopack recommends checking for an available place first.
steps: Check availability with the Dean’s Office.
Collect evidence of the no-fault reason.
Apply for course registration.
Check USOS to confirm registration.
lateRegistration.template:
I request registration outside the system for the subject [name, code, group].
Registration did not happen on time because of [reason beyond my control].
There is a free place in group [code]: [confirmation].

resumption.label: Resuming studies
resumption.title: Returning is possible, but not in every situation
resumption.summary: The Dean may permit resumption within 3 years after removal from the student list if none of the §22 barriers applies. Resumption may involve programme differences and a different starting semester.
checklist: No outstanding obligations to the University
Supervisor’s approval when returning only for defence
steps: Check the barriers listed in §22.
Discuss the possible semester with the Dean’s Office.
Submit with supporting documents.
After approval, check programme differences and deadlines.
resumption.template:
I request resumption of studies in [programme] from semester [proposed semester].
I was removed from the student list on [date] because of [reason].
Reason for returning: [description].

leave.label: Leave from classes
leave.title: Apply as soon as the reason arises
leave.summary: Leave may be short- or long-term and may concern health, education, parenthood, financial hardship or an unexpected event. It cannot be granted for a completed semester.
steps: For a short absence, contact teachers first.
Define the leave period needed.
Apply immediately after the reason arises.
After the decision, check classes and how differences are made up.
leave.template:
I request [short-/long-term] leave from classes from [date] to [date] because [reason].
I attach [document].

promoter.label: Changing thesis supervisor
promoter.title: A change also depends on seminar capacity
promoter.summary: §41 allows the Dean to approve a supervisor change. The Infopack adds practical requirements: checking capacity, opinions from both supervisors and a 30-day deadline from the start of the final seminar semester.
checklist: Available place with the target supervisor
steps: Ask the Dean’s Office about capacity.
Speak to both supervisors.
Obtain their opinions.
Apply early in the semester.
promoter.template:
I request permission to change my thesis supervisor from [name] to [name].
Grounds: [reason].
I attach both opinions and confirmation of capacity.

appeal.label: Appealing a decision
appeal.title: You may appeal an adverse decision to the Rector
appeal.deadline: You appeal within 7 days of receiving the decision
appeal.summary: Current §13 names the Rector as the appeal authority. The appeal needs grounds and is submitted directly to the Rector through USOS.
steps: Read the reasons and appeal notice.
Calculate the 7-day deadline.
State what should be revoked or changed.
Submit a reasoned appeal through USOS.
appeal.template:
I appeal the decision dated [date] concerning [subject].
I request that it be [revoked/changed].
Grounds: [objections, new facts, documents].

multiple.q: Can I receive several benefits at once?
multiple.a: Yes, if you meet the conditions of each. One limit: the social and Rector's scholarships together cannot exceed 38% of a professor's salary. If the total is higher, you get the full social scholarship and the Rector's scholarship is reduced accordingly.

diff.q: How does a hardship grant differ from a social scholarship?
diff.a: A hardship grant is one-off help in a sudden, temporarily difficult life event, awarded independently of the social scholarship.

odmowa.q: My application was refused. What can I do?
odmowa.a: You have 14 days from receiving the decision. Against a decision of the Scholarship Committee you appeal to the Appeals Scholarship Committee (through the Scholarship Committee); against a decision of the Rector you request a reconsideration. The instructions at the end of the decision say which applies to you. If you need help, contact the Student Ombudsman.

dwaKierunki.q: I study two programmes. On which one do I get a scholarship?
dwaKierunki.a: You receive benefits on one programme only - the one you choose. If you also get a decision on another programme or at another university, you have 7 days from receiving it to resign from one of them.

spozniony.q: I missed the deadline. Can I still apply?
spozniony.a: Only if the delay was not your fault. Within 7 days of the cause ending, request reinstatement of the deadline, show it was not your fault, and attach the scholarship application itself.

stypRektora.metaDesc: The Rector's scholarship of the Wroclaw University of Economics and Business for outstanding academic results and scientific, artistic and sporting achievements. Who can get it and how to apply via USOSweb.
stypRektora.heroLead: For outstanding academic results and scientific, artistic or sporting achievements at least at national level.
stypRektora.heading: Who can get it
stypRektora.intro: The Rector's scholarship goes to students with outstanding academic results, scientific or artistic achievements, or sporting results in competitions at least at national level. You apply from 21 to 31 October. The detailed criteria and scoring are set out in Annex 3 to the Benefits Regulations for Students.

notes.title: What counts
notes.desc: The arithmetic average of your grades from the last two semesters - at least 4.00 - excluding seminars, physical education and internships. Plus documented scientific, artistic and sporting achievements. For the average you get as many points as its decimal part (e.g. 4.57 gives 57 points), and each recognised achievement adds points.

notes.title: At most 10% of a programme
notes.desc: Each programme has its own ranking list. The scholarship goes to no more than 10% of the programme's students - those with the most points.

notes.title: First year of studies
notes.desc: In the first year of first-cycle studies, the scholarship goes to international olympiad laureates, central-level olympiad laureates and finalists, and medallists of at least the Polish Championship - if admitted in the year they passed the matura. In the first year of second-cycle studies, your average and achievements from the last two semesters of first-cycle studies count.

notes.title: Who cannot apply
notes.desc: A student who is repeating a semester or waiting to repeat it, is conditionally enrolled, did not pass the previous year by the end of the exam session, or has been suspended from scholarships as a disciplinary penalty.

notes.title: UEW Own Scholarship Fund scholarship
notes.desc: Besides the Rector's scholarship, in some years the University awards a one-off scholarship for a high average from the UEW Own Scholarship Fund. Details are below, in the section on that scholarship.

stypSocjalne.metaDesc: A social scholarship for UEW students in a more difficult financial situation - how to apply via USOSweb, what documentation to prepare and what to remember.
stypSocjalne.heroLead: For students in a difficult financial situation. The award depends on income per person, calculated under the Benefits Regulations for Students.
stypSocjalne.heading: So that money does not get in the way of your studies
stypSocjalne.intro: The social scholarship is available to students in a difficult financial situation. What counts is income per person, calculated under the Benefits Regulations for Students. The income threshold is set by law (45% of the minimum wage); the meter below shows the current amount.

notes.title: Applying for the first time?
notes.desc: First-time applicants must submit a printed, signed application together with an income declaration and full documentation confirming income.

notes.title: Adult sibling who is studying
notes.desc: If you have an adult sibling who is studying, attach a current certificate of continued education to your summer-semester application.

notes.title: Change in family situation
notes.desc: Report changes such as a death, the birth of a child, an adult sibling finishing their education or getting married - they affect the amount of the benefit.

notes.title: An application before each semester
notes.desc: The social scholarship is awarded per semester, so you apply twice a year: for the winter semester from 25 September to 8 October, for the summer semester from 7 to 21 March.

notes.title: Increased scholarship
notes.desc: In particularly justified cases you can receive a higher social scholarship if you give reasons and document them. The increase is set by the Rector in agreement with the Student Government.

One condition: you have a stable source of income and your average monthly income in the previous tax year and in the current year is at least {amount}. Others include being 26 or older, being married, supporting a child, or having reached adulthood in foster care (Section 15(2) of the Benefits Regulations for Students). You then count only your own, your spouse's and your children's income.

stypNiepelnosprawni.metaDesc: A scholarship for UEW students with a certified disability - how to apply via USOSweb and what certificate to attach.
stypNiepelnosprawni.heroLead: Support for students with a certified disability - independent of financial situation and of other benefits.
stypNiepelnosprawni.heading: A benefit independent of income
stypNiepelnosprawni.intro: The scholarship is available to students who hold a current disability certificate. It does not depend on your financial situation and can be received alongside other benefits. You apply from 1 October to 15 June.

notes.title: Which certificate counts
notes.desc: A disability certificate, a certificate of the degree of disability (mild, moderate or severe), or a certificate from a ZUS medical examiner that the law treats as equivalent. Attach the questionnaire from the document list. If the certificate expires during the year, the scholarship is paid until it expires - with a new certificate, submit a new application.

notes.title: The amount depends on the degree
notes.desc: The higher the degree of disability, the higher the scholarship. If the certificate does not state a degree, it counts as mild. The amounts are set by the Rector in agreement with the Student Government.

zapomoga.metaDesc: A hardship grant is one-off help for UEW students who find themselves in a sudden, temporarily difficult life situation. How to apply via USOSweb.
zapomoga.heroLead: One-off help for students who, for reasons beyond their control, find themselves in a temporarily difficult life situation.
zapomoga.heading: Immediate support in a sudden situation
zapomoga.intro: A hardship grant is a one-off benefit when you temporarily find yourself in a difficult life situation, e.g. after the death of someone close, during a serious illness, after a fire or flood, or after the birth of a child. You get it independently of the social scholarship.

notes.title: When to apply
notes.desc: Without delay, no later than 3 months after the event (applications are accepted from 1 October to 15 September). Attach evidence, e.g. invoices in your name, medical certificates, or certificates from an office or the police. For a serious illness, an opinion from a medical specialist is required.

notes.title: At most twice a year
notes.desc: You can receive a hardship grant no more than twice in an academic year, and only once for the same reason.

fuePsrp.metaDesc: The Student Government of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business is part of the Forum of Economic Universities and the Students' Parliament of the Republic of Poland. See how we represent students beyond the University.
fuePsrp.heroLead: We represent the students of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business beyond the University as well: together with the student governments of other universities of economics and in the Students' Parliament of the Republic of Poland.
fuePsrp.fueBody: An alliance of the student governments of Poland's public universities of economics, which for over 15 years has represented their students in the Students' Parliament. The Forum oversees joint projects: Economic Bridges, the Economic Knowledge Test and Transekonomik.
fuePsrp.psrpBody: The statutory representative of all students in Poland. It represents them before state authorities, gives opinions on higher-education legislation and trains student governments. Our Chair represents us at Parliament meetings, and our delegates vote at the PSRP Convention, which elects the Chair of the Parliament.
fuePsrp.heroPhotoAlt: Students of Wroclaw University of Economics and Business outside Poznań Główny station on their way to the Economic Bridges exchange
fuePsrp.zjazdHeading: Meeting of the Forum of Economic Universities
fuePsrp.zjazdBody: Forum meetings bring together representatives of the student governments of economics universities from Warsaw, Kraków, Katowice, Poznań and Wrocław. Over three days they discuss the Forum's affairs, share experience and decide how to develop their joint projects: Economic Bridges, the Economic Knowledge Test and Transekonomik. The host of the next meeting is chosen during the session.
fuePsrp.zjazdTeam: When Wrocław hosts, the meeting is prepared by a Student Government team, from rooms on campus to the programme for guests. We announce team recruitment on the Recruitment page.

deklaracja.metaDesc: Digital accessibility statement for the SSUEW Student Government website - WCAG 2.1 conformance, the complaints procedure and contact details.
deklaracja.heroLead: The Student Government of Wrocław University of Economics and Business is committed to the digital accessibility of this site in line with the Polish Digital Accessibility Act of 4 April 2019.
deklaracja.metaDate: Statement prepared on: 26 June 2026. Last reviewed: 30 July 2026. Method: self-assessment by the public body, supported by an automated tool (axe-core) and a code review.
deklaracja.intro: The site is designed to WCAG 2.1 level AA, and in many places AAA: sufficient contrast, visible focus, full keyboard support, semantic headings, text alternatives and respect for reduced-motion preferences.

sections.title: Conformance status
sections.body: The site is partially conformant with the Digital Accessibility Act - it meets WCAG 2.1 level AA within the scope covered by the audit carried out. The audit of 30 July 2026 combined automated testing (45/45 axe-core scans, zero violations) with a code review (contrast, keyboard operation and focus, semantics, forms, touch targets ≥ 44 px); every issue found was fixed. Exclusions - elements not yet verified: (1) how the site is experienced through a screen reader (an NVDA/VoiceOver session is planned - automated tests and code review do not replace it), (2) the accessibility of PDF documents and photo alt texts that will be published on the site in future. Each of these will undergo a separate accessibility review, and this statement will be updated accordingly.

sections.title: Keyboard support & aids
sections.body: You can navigate the site with the keyboard (Tab / Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc). A “skip to content” link, clearly visible focus and a search opened with Ctrl/⌘ + K are available. The site respects the system reduced-motion setting (prefers-reduced-motion) and works in light and dark mode.

sections.title: Feedback and complaints procedure
sections.body: Anyone has the right to request that the website or an element of it be made accessible. Send your request to kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl, indicating the page concerned and a convenient form of contact. If accessibility cannot be ensured, we will propose alternative access. If a request is refused, you may file a complaint with the supervising authority and a petition to the Ombudsman.

sections.title: Architectural accessibility
sections.body: Student Government office: ul. Kamienna 44, Building L, room 110, 53-307 Wrocław. Detailed information about the building’s architectural accessibility (entrance, lifts, parking, access for assistance-dog users) is available on request - write to kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

prywatnosc.metaDesc: How the SSUEW Student Government processes data on this site - contact form, analytics, cookies and your rights (GDPR).
prywatnosc.heroLead: We explain what data we process on this site, why, and what rights you have.

sections.title: Data controller
sections.body: The data controller is Wroclaw University of Economics and Business, ul. Komandorska 118/120, 53-345 Wrocław. The forms and mailboxes are run by the UEW Student Government. For data matters, write to: kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

sections.title: What data we process
sections.body: Site forms (contact, Student Ombudsman, partnerships): your name or organisation name, email address and message - solely to respond to your enquiry. Submissions go to a Google Sheet and to the Student Government mailbox within the University’s Google account - no external form relay is involved. Member login uses a Google account in the @samorzad.ue.wroc.pl domain; we only store a technical session in a necessary cookie.

sections.title: Data processors
sections.body: Our forms are handled by a Google Apps Script running on the Student Government account inside the University’s Google Workspace. A submission is stored in a Google Sheet and delivered to the mailbox belonging to that form. The University remains the controller; Google acts as a processor under the agreement held by the University. Only the content you type into the form reaches the script. The Student Ombudsman form may concern sensitive matters - those submissions go to a separate mailbox, and if you would rather skip the form entirely, write directly to rps@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl. The site is hosted on Vercel (Vercel Inc.), which processes the server logs necessary to operate it.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.body: Necessary cookies (a logged-in member’s session and your language preference) always work - they are required for the site to function. Analytics cookies and scripts run only with your consent; you can change your choice at any time by clearing the site’s data in your browser.

sections.title: Analytics
sections.body: We use Vercel Web Analytics - anonymous, aggregated visit statistics. It uses no cookies and does not identify individuals. We collect it only if you consent.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, rectify, erase or restrict the processing of your data, as well as the right to object and to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (in Poland: the President of the Personal Data Protection Office). We keep contact-form data only as long as needed to handle your case.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Send privacy and data questions to: kontakt@samorzad.ue.wroc.pl.

wydawnictwo.metaDesc: Debiuty Studenckie is a series by the Wrocław University of Economics and Business Press for first- and second-year students. Open access, CC BY-SA 4.0.
wydawnictwo.heroLead: A paper from a course or a research circle can become a real publication, with an ISBN and open access. The bar is lower than you think.
wydawnictwo.aboutIntro: Debiuty Studenckie is a series published by the Wrocław University of Economics and Business Press, which has been operating since 1955 and puts out more than 100 titles a year. The series is addressed directly to student research circles: a place where a paper, article or chapter written in a circle can become a real publication.

years.title: Year I or II is enough
years.desc: The authors are first- and second-year students. You don't need to wait for your master's thesis or have a research track record. A text worth showing is enough.

license.title: CC BY-SA 4.0, no hidden barriers
license.desc: Every publication is released in open access under a Creative Commons licence. You can freely share it, cite it, and build on it.

circles.title: Made for research circles
circles.desc: The series is addressed directly to student research circles: a natural place to turn a circle's project into a real publication with an ISBN.

layout.desc: After a positive review, the text goes through editorial layout and is assigned an ISBN.

publish.title: Publication in open access
publish.desc: The finished publication is released in open access under CC BY-SA 4.0, available to everyone free of charge.

stypFundusz.heading: A one-off scholarship for a high grade average
stypFundusz.intro: A separate scholarship the University pays from its own fund once a year. Only your average counts: every exam and course grade from the last academic year (1 October to 30 September), fails included. Every recipient gets the same amount, up to PLN 10,000.

steps.title: Check the threshold for your programme
steps.desc: When the Rector opens a call (by an order issued by 15 October), it sets the minimum average for each programme and the email addresses to send applications to.

steps.title: Send the application from your university email
steps.desc: Send the completed application (the template is in the BIP) from your University mailbox by 30 November. Late applications are not considered.

steps.title: Wait for the ranking
steps.desc: Applications are assessed by a committee that includes a Student Government representative. The Rector awards scholarships based on the average ranking.

notes.title: Have academic achievements? Attach them
notes.desc: When several people have the same average and there is not enough money for all, academic achievements decide: publications, an award for a thesis in an external competition, or a conference presentation confirmed by an abstract. Attach copies of the pages showing the author, title, date of publication and ISBN/ISSN, or a confirmation from the publisher. If you list an achievement without a document, the committee will not consider the whole application.

notes.title: There is not a call every year
notes.desc: If the fund holds less than PLN 100,000 on 30 September, the Rector does not open a call that academic year.
